Finding round: **graded, promoted to `pm:queue`**, `finding` shed. **`domain:ui`** (`packages/plugin-dashboard`, published-library stream). Type **Task**: removing a written-never-read member is behaviour-preserving — no reader exists to notice — so nothing declared is violated and nothing widens.

Straightforward enforce-or-remove, and the measurement is done properly: **zero `.decimals` member reads** across `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/core` and `plugin-dashboard`, with a **positive control in the same query shape** (`.scale` member reads hit in `NumberField.tsx`, `GridField.tsx`, `index.tsx`). ⇒ The zero is a finding, not a broken query.

⛔ **The band coupling is a hard fence, and it is the whole risk of this card** — a naive grep-clean would silently un-enforce a ruling that landed today. `AuthoredColumnOverrides`' refusal band derives from **`keyof FieldMeta`**, so `decimals`' membership in that band is what enforces the #6425 retire **at the read site**, pinned by `ObjectDataTable.overrideSource-6425.test.tsx`. Removing `FieldMeta.decimals` therefore removes it from the band as a side effect.

⇒ The dispatch must require: **keep an explicit refusal for the authored `decimals` key**, or update that pin **deliberately and say so**. ⛔ Do not let the pin go green by the key ceasing to exist — a pin that passes because its subject was deleted is the "green while blind" shape this fleet keeps filing. If the dev finds no way to preserve the refusal without keeping the member, **stop and report** rather than choosing.

⚠️ **Premise to re-verify on the merged ref**: measured on a worktree at `c63f6913` (base `2a23000f`), and **#6425 closed at 2026-08-27T20:20:03Z** — during this triage round. So the retire has now landed on `main` and the file state has moved. Re-read `recordFields.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and the pin against the post-merge tree; ⛔ do not implement from this card's quoted state.

**Scope as filed**: retire `FieldMeta.decimals` and the now-unfed `BuildFieldMetaParams.overrides.decimals` **together** — `ObjectDataTable.enrich()` no longer passes it and `RecordDetailDrawer` never did, so the parameter has no feeder left. ⭐ And the card's forward note is right: if a reader is ever intended, it should read **`scale`** like the rest of the family, ⛔ not resurrect `decimals`.

⭐ Correctly filed rather than ridden along: #6425's dispatch fence named `ObjectDataTable.tsx` plus types and tests, and `recordFields.tsx` sits outside it — and the ruling adjudicated the **authored column key**, not `FieldMeta`'s own member. Two different subjects one layer apart.

Family: #6425 (the ruling, now landed), #6373 (the write half of the same seam), #6597 (`referenceTo`, the promised-but-not-kept sibling) — worth a glance at #6597 when this is picked up, since a second dead member in the same type may fold into one PR.

Claim: `domain:ui` execution seat, session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c`, branch `claude/issue-6625-retire-fieldmeta-decimals`.

## The whole risk of this card is one coupling, and it is the reason this is not a grep-clean

`AuthoredColumnOverrides`' refusal band derives from **`keyof FieldMeta`**. So `decimals`' membership in `FieldMeta` is what enforces the #6425 retire **at the read site**, pinned by `ObjectDataTable.overrideSource-6425.test.tsx`. Deleting the member removes it from the band as a side effect — and the pin then passes **because its subject stopped existing**, not because the refusal still holds.

⛔ **Do not let that pin go green by deletion.** Either keep an explicit refusal for the authored `decimals` key, or update the pin **deliberately and say so in the PR body**. If you find no way to preserve the refusal without keeping the member, **stop and report** rather than choosing — that fork is mine, not yours.

This is the same mechanism this lane measured twice this week from the other direction: a pin whose enforcement rides on a key's *non*-membership silently stops enforcing the moment the key becomes a member. Here it rides on *membership* and stops the moment the member is deleted. Nothing goes red at the moment of loss in either direction, which is why it has to be handled deliberately rather than discovered.

## ⚠️ Re-verify on the merged ref — do NOT implement from the card's quoted state

The card's measurements were taken on a worktree at `c63f6913`, and **#6425 closed 2026-08-27T20:20:03Z, during that triage round**. The retire has landed on `main` since. Re-read `recordFields.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and the pin against the **current** `origin/main` before touching anything; if the post-merge tree contradicts the card, report that rather than reconciling it silently.

## Scope

Retire `FieldMeta.decimals` **together with** the now-unfed `BuildFieldMetaParams.overrides.decimals` — `ObjectDataTable.enrich()` no longer passes it and `RecordDetailDrawer` never did, so the parameter has no feeder left. Both halves in one PR, so the key leaves in one move.

⛔ Do not add a reader. If a reader is ever wanted here it should read **`scale`** like the rest of the family — reviving `decimals` is the wrong direction and is explicitly out of scope.

## On the sibling card

#6597 (`referenceTo` — promised in the README, kept by nothing) is a second dead member in the same type and may fold cleanly into one PR. **Do not fold it yourself** — it is a separate `pm:queue` card that is not claimed, and folding it would cross into unclaimed work. If it genuinely folds, say so in your report with what you'd need, and I'll make that call.

## Verification

- The zero that justifies this card was measured with a positive control (`.scale` member reads hitting `NumberField.tsx`, `GridField.tsx`, `index.tsx`). **Re-establish that zero yourself on the current tree, in the same query shape with the same control** — a zero inherited from a stale ref is not a measurement.
- Type-check every package whose surface the removal touches, not only the one you edited.
- Run `ObjectDataTable.overrideSource-6425.test.tsx` and state explicitly, in words, *why* it passes after your change — "the refusal is still enforced by X" or "the pin was deliberately updated to Y". A bare green is not an answer here.
- Changeset: this removes members from a published type. Follow the repo's changeset policy and let the gates rule the bump; if a gate refuses the honest declaration, **stop and report** — ⛔ never re-score a breaking removal down to satisfy a gate.
- Re-read your diff adversarially before pushing.

Draft PR, `Fixes #6625`.

ACCEPT — PR #6636, flipped ready and armed for the queue.

**Entry qualification, head `c16891e0`:** 29 checks, 29 returned against `total_count: 29`. **26 success, 3 skipped, zero failures, zero cancelled, zero still running.**

## The fork did not need me, and that is the right outcome

My order said: keep an explicit refusal, or update the pin deliberately and say so, or stop and report. The refusal is preserved **without** keeping the member — a hand-written `ObjectDataTableRetiredDecimalsTombstone` carries #6425's verdict now, following `ObjectGridRetiredOptionsTombstone`'s precedent in `plugin-grid`. No pin was weakened, so no fork arose.

## ⭐ My fence named one band; there are two

I wrote that `AuthoredColumnOverrides`' refusal band derives from `keyof FieldMeta`. So does **`EnrichedColumn`'s write-side tombstone band** (#6373), from the same pool. Deleting the member would have silently un-enforced the retire at **both** ends of the seam, not one. The tombstone is intersected into both halves "because the retirement belongs to the SEAM, not to one of its two halves".

**Lane rule from this, and it generalises past this card:** this repo has *two* seam bands derived from `keyof FieldMeta`, and a dispatch fence naming only one under-describes the blast radius of touching any member. That is my error to carry forward, not the dev's to have guessed around.

## ⭐ The pin was already blind, and the ablation proves the fix is load-bearing

The existing `@ts-expect-error` assigned a **fresh object literal**, which the excess-property check refuses whether or not any tombstone exists — so it pinned "something refused this" without pinning *what*, and would have gone on passing after the member was deleted. Changed to a non-fresh variable, which skips the freshness check and reaches only the tombstone.

Then it proved the tombstone is what answers, rather than asserting it. Neutralising the tombstone to an empty object type yields **exit 2** with TS2578 "unused `ts-expect-error`" at *both* pin suites plus a TS2339 — so without it, those pins really would have passed because their subject stopped existing. Mutation confirmed on disk by anchored greps in both directions plus a blob-hash move, never by an editor's exit code; restore proven by hash-back plus empty `git diff HEAD`.

**And the second ablation leg is the one worth keeping.** On that same ablated tree the **runtime suites stayed green** — 2 files, 22 tests, exit 0 — because `ts-expect-error` is type-erased. The blindness is one-sided: only `tsc` sees it, and a passing test run sees nothing at all. For this class of pin, a green test run is not evidence; the type-check is the only instrument.

## It corrected my dispatch order, with a measurement

I called this "removing members from a published type". Measured: it isn't. `FieldMeta`, `BuildFieldMetaParams`, `AuthoredColumnOverrides` and `EnrichedColumn` are absent from `dist/index.d.ts`, not re-exported by the barrel, and `exports` publishes only the root entry — no consumer can name them. That is what makes `minor` honest here rather than a downgrade to satisfy a gate, and it is measured rather than argued.

## The #6597 fold question, answered correctly

Mechanically it folds — same evidence shape, same type, same coupling, ~15 lines. **Decisionally it does not:** #6597 is enforce-or-remove with two live branches, and folding would silently pick the removal branch, which is the ruling that card exists to obtain. Stopping there was right. The analysis is recorded on #6597 so it is not re-derived.

Closure will be confirmed from `closed_by_pull_requests` after the merge, not assumed from the `Fixes` line.
